title: The Iceberg Document: correlated priors and independent discovery channels
description: The largest group, from the Iceberg Document, the selection metrology programme and the anomaly-trigger inversion battery, holds that shared representational priors across instruments, corpora and classifiers erode the independent channels through which anomalies were historically saved, and that Kuhn's account presupposed an anomaly-retention infrastructure. It sets tests for noncoverage estimators on LHC anomaly triggers and forecasts measurable assimilation-to-unfundable where embedding-based novelty scoring enters grant triage. Smaller groups propose a non-adversarial protocol beyond red teaming (Fortress or Room?), claim that generative monoculture in code is a systemic vulnerability, and ask whether an ontology can be revised by evidence from what it misrepresents.
